title: Responsive Design & Content Reflow 📐
description: Build layouts that adapt gracefully, support zoom, and never lose content or functionality on small screens.

slides.title: Responsive = Accessible 💧
slides.content:
A responsive layout that reflows for different screen sizes is inherently more accessible. It ensures:

- Content is readable without zooming at 320px width.
- Text can be resized to 200% without loss of information or functionality (WCAG 1.4.4).
- Horizontal scrolling is not required.

Flexbox and CSS Grid make responsive design easier than ever. Use relative units (%, `rem`, `vw`) instead of fixed pixels.

quizData.question: What is the minimum viewport width you should design for to support 200% zoom on a 1280px screen?
quizData.explanation: At 400% zoom, 1280px wide becomes 320px; WCAG requires 200% but designing for 320px covers the worst case.

slides.title: Reflow & Scroll‑direction 🧭
slides.content:
Content must reflow to fit the viewport without requiring two‑directional scrolling. Vertical scrolling is fine; horizontal scrolling is not.

- Use `max‑width: 100%` on images and containers.
- Avoid fixed‑width layouts; use `min()` and `clamp()`.
- Test with a device that is 320px wide (iPhone 5/SE).
- Ensure that zoom does not cause overlapping or cut‑off text.

Think of reflow as water: content should fill the container naturally.

slides.title: Responsive Text & Container

quizData.question: At 200% zoom, a paragraph of text overflows its container and a horizontal scrollbar appears. Is this a WCAG AA failure?

options.text: Yes, because content is lost and two‑directional scrolling is needed
No, as long as the text is still readable

quizData.explanation: WCAG 1.4.10 Reflow requires no horizontal scrolling at 320px equivalent width.

slides.title: Orientation & Screen Lock 📱↔️
slides.content:
WCAG 1.3.4 Orientation: Content must not restrict its view to a single orientation (unless essential, like a piano app).

- Your site must work in both portrait and landscape.
- Avoid CSS that locks orientation via `@media (orientation: landscape) { /* only styles */ }` without providing a portrait fallback.
- Consider users who mount devices in a fixed orientation on a wheelchair.

Test by rotating your phone.

quizData.question: A mobile website shows a message 'Please rotate your device to landscape'. Is this a WCAG violation?

options.text: Yes, unless landscape orientation is essential for the content
Only if the message is inaccessible

quizData.explanation: WCAG 1.3.4 prohibits restricting to a single orientation unless essential.

slides.title: Mobile Navigation Patterns 🧭
slides.content:
Hamburger menus, tab bars, and bottom navigation are common. Ensure:

- The toggle button for a menu has `aria-expanded` and an accessible name.
- Focus moves into the menu when opened and back to the toggle when closed.
- Swipe gestures to open a drawer should have a visible alternative (like a button).
- Bottom navigation should be easy to reach with a thumb.

Design for thumb reach: key actions at the bottom of the screen.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Use `viewport` meta tag correctly
`<meta name="viewport" content="width=device‑width, initial‑scale=1">` ensures mobile browsers don't shrink your layout.
